headline_marked: Dhaka: [[Land grabbing and extortion surge]] as mobs use heavy machinery
headline: Dhaka: Land grabbing and extortion surge as mobs use heavy machinery
summary: Four major attacks in three days have highlighted a troubling new pattern of organized violence and land theft in the capital.
details: Four attacks in just three days involving land disputes, land grabs, and looting in Dhaka have revealed a troubling new pattern of organized violence.
Groups of dozens to hundreds of people have been forcing their way onto properties, vandalizing structures, and using heavy machinery like bulldozers to raze buildings to the ground.
Recent incidents occurred at the Radda health centre in Mirpur, an office in Chand Udyan, a building in Shekhertek, and a New Gini Properties project in Manikdi.
Victims report that buildings under construction have become routine targets for extortion, with demands for money being made even for the removal of rubble.
One banker described how he and partners were forced off their own eight-storey building in Bosila Garden City after a group of 40-50 people took over the property.
Police have arrested 13 people in connection with attacks in Mohammadpur and Adabor, while Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed has vowed that no criminal will be spared.
Site engineers and contractors report that land-related extortion has reached alarming levels, particularly in rapidly developing areas of Mirpur and Mohammadpur.
caption:
Bulldozers and mobs of hundreds are now being used to seize land in Dhaka. Victims say their lifetime savings are buried in stolen properties.

Recent incidents occurred at the Radda health centre in Mirpur, an office in Chand Udyan, a building in Shekhertek, and a New Gini Properties project in Manikdi.

One banker described how he and partners were forced off their own eight-storey building in Bosila Garden City after a group of 40-50 people took over the property.

Police have arrested 13 people in connection with attacks in Mohammadpur and Adabor, while Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed has vowed that no criminal will be spared.

headline_marked: Pakistan airspace denial delays [[Rooppur nuclear fuel shipments]] to October
headline: Pakistan airspace denial delays Rooppur nuclear fuel shipments to October
summary: Russian state nuclear corporation Rosatom announced that uranium fuel for the plant's second unit will now arrive between October and December.
details: Uranium fuel shipments for the second unit of the Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant will begin arriving in Bangladesh from October, according to Russian state nuclear corporation Rosatom.
The delivery was delayed after a transport aircraft from Russia was denied airspace overflight clearance by Pakistan, despite all logistical preparations being complete.
The shipment was originally scheduled to arrive on September 24 to refuel the first unit of the nuclear power station.
Kabir Hossain, project director, stated that 48 fuel assemblies were expected on two flights, scheduled for September 24 and October 1.
The initial fuel load for Unit 2 was planned to arrive via seven weekly flights starting October 8.
Under the revised schedule, flights will now begin on October 1, pushing the timeline back by one week.
The air route for these shipments typically passes through the airspace of Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, Afghanistan, Pakistan, and India.
Rosatom clarified that the fuel for the second unit will be delivered across several flights in full compliance with contractual terms and the project timeline.
caption:
A denied overflight clearance from Pakistan has delayed critical nuclear fuel shipments for the Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant.

Uranium fuel shipments for the second unit of the Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant will begin arriving in Bangladesh from October, according to Russian state nuclear corporation Rosatom.

The delivery was delayed after a transport aircraft from Russia was denied airspace overflight clearance by Pakistan, despite all logistical preparations being complete.

The shipment was originally scheduled to arrive on September 24 to refuel the first unit of the nuclear power station.

Kabir Hossain, project director, stated that 48 fuel assemblies were expected on two flights, scheduled for September 24 and October 1.

The initial fuel load for Unit 2 was planned to arrive via seven weekly flights starting October 8.

Under the revised schedule, flights will now begin on October 1, pushing the timeline back by one week.

The air route for these shipments typically passes through the airspace of Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, Afghanistan, Pakistan, and India.

Rosatom clarified that the fuel for the second unit will be delivered across several flights in full compliance with contractual terms and the project timeline.
